summary: Nigeria moved its short-visit visas fully online in May 2025: most nationalities now apply for an e-Visa (tourism or business), replacing the old visa-on-arrival scheme, while ECOWAS citizens continue to enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

declarations.text: In response to the Ebola outbreak, travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission must complete the free online Nigeria Health Declaration Form before boarding; the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, which runs the form, says passengers from all other countries are exempt at this time. notes: The UK Foreign Office says possession or use of illegal drugs, including cannabis, carries severe penalties, with long jail sentences and heavy fines also for smuggling and when transiting.
It is illegal to export African art, particularly antiques, without written authorisation from the Department of Antiquities, according to the UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada.

The UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada say it is illegal to import beer, mineral water, soft drinks, sparkling wine, fruits, vegetables, cereals, eggs, textile fabrics, jewellery or precious metals.

payments.text: The Government of Canada describes Nigeria's economy as cash-based: US dollars are widely accepted, ATMs are not widely available outside major cities, and credit cards are accepted at some major hotels in Abuja and Lagos — though it advises avoiding credit and debit cards because of the high potential for fraud. The UK Foreign Office warns of a spike in crime around banks and ATMs.

safety.text: Risk varies sharply by state. Lagos, Abuja and much of the south-west are visited routinely with sensible precautions, but the FCDO advises against all travel to Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, Katsina and Zamfara states and to the riverine areas of the Niger Delta, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the north, the Middle Belt and parts of the south-east, because of terrorism, banditry and kidnapping. Plan state by state against current advisories.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The Government of Canada says the rainy season runs from May to October, with flash and seasonal flooding that can make roads impassable. The dry season, November to April, brings periodic heat waves well above 40°C, especially in central and northern Nigeria, and the dusty Harmattan wind, typically November to March and strongest from December to February, which reduces visibility and air quality.

tips.text: Apply for the e-Visa only through the Nigeria Immigration Service's official portal, evisa.immigration.gov.ng, linked from immigration.gov.ng.

Check advice for each state on your route, not just the national rating: the UK Foreign Office advises against all or all but essential travel to parts of the North East, North West, North Central, South East and South South regions. It also advises limiting travel after dark outside city centres, and the Government of Canada advises avoiding all unnecessary travel after dark.
Complete the free digital Landing Card before you fly and the Exit Card before you leave, on the Nigeria Immigration Service portal — travellers who do not can be refused entry or departure.

Take extra care when withdrawing or changing money: the UK Foreign Office reports a spike in criminal activity around banks and ATMs, especially at night, and says credit card fraud is common, so keep your card in sight when paying.
Carry your yellow fever certificate: Nigeria requires proof of vaccination from arriving travellers, except infants aged 8 months or younger and adults aged 61 or older.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Nigeria?
faq.answer: Most travelers do. Since May 2025 short tourist and business visits are handled through Nigeria's official e-Visa, open to more than 180 nationalities including the US, UK, Canada and the EU. ECOWAS citizens enter without a visa under the bloc's free-movement protocol, as do citizens of Cameroon and Chad under visa-abolition agreements, and a small number of nationalities must still apply at a Nigerian embassy.

faq.question: Does Nigeria still issue visas on arrival?
faq.answer: No. The visa-on-arrival scheme was discontinued when the e-Visa launched on May 1, 2025. You must be approved online before boarding. Previously issued VOA approvals expired at the end of May 2025.

faq.question: How long does the Nigeria e-Visa take?
faq.answer: The Nigeria Immigration Service does not publish a processing time for the e-Visa, and no official source states one. The approval arrives by email. Apply well ahead of travel in case additional checks are needed.

faq.question: Can US citizens get a Nigeria e-Visa?
faq.answer: Yes — US passport holders are eligible for the e-Visa for tourism or business, applying online at evisa.immigration.gov.ng.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Nigeria?
faq.answer: Yes. Nigeria requires proof of yellow fever vaccination from arriving travelers, whichever country they come from; only infants aged 8 months or younger and adults aged 61 or older are exempt. Carry the certificate with your passport.

faq.question: What is the Nigeria Landing Card?
faq.answer: A free digital arrival/departure declaration run by the Nigeria Immigration Service since May 2025. Every foreign traveler completes the Landing Card online before arrival and an Exit Card before departure; those who do not can be refused entry or departure at immigration checkpoints.
